chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan, from Fuleyh ibn Abi Bakr al-Shaybani, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The constrained false oath bequeaths poverty to the descendants.'

key_terms.الْكَاذِبَةُ: The false/lying — here meaning an oath known by the swearer to be untrue
key_terms.الْيَمِينُ الصَّبُورُ: The constrained oath — a judicially-administered or compelled oath, distinct from a voluntary oath
key_terms.تُورِثُ الْعَقِبَ الْفَقْرَ: Bequeaths poverty to the descendants — a spiritual/generational consequence

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the consequences of a false constrained oath?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a legal-ethical warning about the gravely sinful nature of al-yamin al-sabur — the constrained or court-administered oath — when sworn falsely. In Islamic jurisprudence, al-yamin al-sabur refers to an oath imposed under judicial or social compulsion, carrying greater moral weight than a casual oath. The Imam warns that such false swearing has lasting spiritual consequences, causing poverty to be inherited by one's own progeny. This teaching was addressed to a community needing guidance on the severe consequences of perjury and false testimony in legal settings.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from hannan, from Fuleyh Bin Abu Bakr Al Shaybani who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The impatient false oath inherits the consequence of poverty’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Fianan from Fulayh ibn abu Bakr al-Shaybaniy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Taking an oath which is false and binding causes poverty consequently.’”
